en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kumudadāyaka Bandhujīvaka Chapter 10 I was once a merchant in Benares, Possessing great wealth and abundant grain. At that time, the Teacher of the World, the Buddha, The Fully Enlightened One, appeared in the world. Having heard of the Teacher’s arrival, With a joyful heart, I went to see him. Approaching the Teacher, the Great Sage, I paid homage at his feet and sat to one side. Seated there, I addressed the Teacher: "O Blessed One, please accept my gift. Then the Teacher, the Great Sage, Accepted my offering of a white lotus. Because of that gift of a white lotus, For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms; I was always reborn among the gods. When I passed away from the divine realm, I was reborn in the human world. In every birth, I was wealthy and prosperous, And I always gave white lotuses as offerings. Now, having become a monk under the Buddha, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. By the power of that root of merit, I have reached the state of final peace. Through this gift of a white lotus, I have attained the supreme state. This is the account of the Elder Kumudadāyaka, The tenth in the Bandhujīvaka Chapter.
Not far from the Himavat mountains,
there was a great lake,
covered with lotuses and water lilies.
There, at that time, I was a bird named Kukuttha, whose plumage was as white as a lotus.
Virtuous, endowed with wisdom,
skilled in merit and demerit—
Padumuttara, the knower of the world.
The recipient of offerings,
the Great Sage wandered not far from the river Jātassara.
Having cut a water-born lily,
I brought it to the Great Sage;
having understood my intention, he accepted it.
The Great Sage accepted it.
Having given that gift,
impelled by the root of merit from that white deed (sukkamūla);
For a hundred thousand aeons,
I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
For sixteen hundred aeons...
There were eight lords of men named Varuṇa,
wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Kumudadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend (apadāna) of the elder Kumudadāyaka.
The sixteenth chapter, the Bandhujīvaka Chapter, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
Bandhujīvaka, Tambapupphi,
Vīthika, Kakkārupupphiya;
The Mandārava, the Kadambī, the Sūlaka,
the Nāgapupphiya, the Punnāga,
the Komudī, and the Gāthā.
"Fifty-six have been enumerated."
